short: Raw-waveform front end and BGRU fusion (M06) depart from the usual approach but are standard: they tie MFCC in clean LRW audio (97.7%); noise gains lack repeated runs and use matched babble.
position: The paper [@petridis2018e2e] changes processing (M06): an 18-layer 1D ResNet on the raw waveform replaces spectral audio features, joined to a raw-pixel visual ResNet by concatenation and a two-layer BGRU, trained jointly. The raw-waveform input departs from the usual approach: both LRW audio-visual studies dated before it use spectral features, and 17 later ones inherit the raw waveform (pattern match, Appendix). The verdict is still standard, because the paper shows the departure without repeated runs or a second dataset and it ties a 2-layer MFCC BGRU in clean audio (97.7% each, Table 1); its noise margin is measured against a baseline with no convolutional front end and a longer schedule (§5), so representation, depth and training length change together. The best LRW audio-visual result in the ledger, 98.76% [@ryumin2023sensors], uses log-Mel input. The audio-visual gain under noise holds in direction, but no repeated runs are reported, the same babble noise type and SNR range in training and test (§4.3, §5) and no fusion alternative; "significantly outperforms" (Abstract) has no test behind it. Evaluation (M12) is standard for AVSR.
